title: Hardware-aware bandit for kernel picking using sequence-length telemetry
creator: Aisha Khatri
description: Design and implement a lightweight, online bandit-based heuristic that picks the optimal kernel implementation variant for a request based on (1) the GPU hardware profile, (2) observed sequence-length distribution for the tenant/route, and (3) runtime signals (latency, tail, token-cost). The system should learn per-tenant or per-route kernel preferences while maintaining safe fallbacks and minimizing cold-start regressions. Integrate with existing profiling hooks and the prefix (prefill)/decode scheduler so kernel choice also considers prefill memory pressure and decode latency targets.
acceptance_criteria: Bandit selector integrated into runtime kernel selection code path behind feature flag
Per-route/tenant preference table persisted and updated online with bounded memory footprint
Latency P95 change within ±5% for production-like workload in canary at 20% traffic
Automatic rollback if tail latency regression >10% or token-cost increases >8%
Clear tracing and metrics emitted for choice decisions and confidence scores
notes_and_comments: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with serving/runtime, infra, and telemetry teams. Agreed to prototype as feature-flagged component with offline simulation mode first.
2025-02-18: Engineering spike completed — microbenchmarks show kernel A wins for short sequences on A100 but kernel B better for midsize seqlens on T4 due to memory-bound behavior.
2025-02-24: Design decision: use Contextual Bandit (LinUCB) for cold-start-friendly exploration with decay; persist per-tenant priors in RocksDB-backed store.
2025-02-28: PM feedback: must surface per-tenant cost delta in Console; added telemetry event to link model+route+kernel to cost estimation.
2025-03-02: Design review with Applied ML — agreed to incorporate seqlen histograms sampled from request stream and a sliding window of 10k requests for update frequency trade-offs.
2025-03-05: Implementation WIP — core bandit service skeleton and metrics hooks done; integration test failing on memory leak in simulated prefill path (investigating).
implementation_plan: 1) Build offline simulator that replays seqlen traces and runtime kernel microbenchmarks to verify bandit policy quality
2) Implement light-weight per-route context extractor (GPU type, seqlen-bucket, model-variant, quantization profile)
3) Integrate LinUCB bandit library with runtime decision path behind feature flag
4) Persist policy state in RocksDB per-dataplane with eviction policy and TTL
5) Add safe-guarding rules: minimum sample count before switching, min confidence threshold, and emergency fallback mapping
6) Add telemetry: choice events, reward signals (latency cost + token cost composite), confidence, and rollback triggers
7) E2E tests, load test in staging, and 20% canary rollout followed by ramp to 100% if stable
test_plan: Unit tests for context feature extractor and policy update logic
Offline simulation verifying bandit learns expected kernel for synthetic seqlen distributions
Staging load run: 24h mixed workload with seqlen skew to validate stability and memory usage
Canary: 20% traffic for 48h with automated SLA checks on P50/P95 and token-cost delta
Chaos test: induce GPU throttling and verify graceful fallback to conservative kernel mapping
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal cluster only with synthetic traffic
Beta: staging with production traffic replay for 48h
Canary: 20% of production routes for 48h with auto-rollback policy
Full rollout: 100% after 72h stable canary and cost/latency thresholds met
metrics: Avg token-cost per million tokens (USD) by kernel choice
Kernel switch count per hour (safety metric)
Memory pressure (prefill KV cache usage) per kernel
